newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rebounds on dollar selling by exporters.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rebounds on dollar selling by exporters.

text.p: The ringgit rebounded in late Asian trading on dollar sales by exporters, but dealers said the dollar remained on track to retest its recent high against the ringgit on the back of dollar/majors strength.
"Dollar selling by exporters was stationed around 2.6400 and one large order took it down all the way to 2.6300," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
But ringgit gains were capped by fresh dollar bids from local and offshore players, he said.
He added that thin volumes and wide spreads continued to exaggerate currency movements.
At 0930 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6345/75 to a dollar after hitting a low of 2.6445 early in the day. It closed at 2.6340/70 in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday.

The ringgit had earlier extended its negative tone on the back of an unexpectedly large trade deficit of 2.8 billion ringgit for June, after a surplus of 156.2 million in May, and a weak Malaysian stock market.
Dealers said the recent swaps restriction was not having its desired effect on the dollar/ringgit.
"The swaps restriction will not be effective for a while as the market is well funded," said a dealer with a European bank in Singapore.
He said the market was already long on ringgit positions and offshore players accounted for the bulk of liquidity in the forward market.

Bank Negara ordered local banks to limit non-trade related currency swaps to $2.0 million with each overseas customer from Monday as part of an effort to cool speculation in the ringgit and bring down interest rates.

Dealers said given its bullish sentiment, the dollar could retest its recent high of 2.6530 against the ringgit. But the market will be watching for possible central bank intervention at the 2.6500 level, they said.
